events.title: The Council of Pisa elects a third claimant
events.shortBlurb: Seeking to end the Western Schism, the council deposed two rival popes and elected a third, deepening the crisis…
body: The Western Schism had divided Latin Christendom since 1378 between rival lines of popes at Rome and Avignon, each with its own obedience of kingdoms and cardinals. To end the scandal, cardinals of both sides gathered in a council at Pisa in 1409, declared both claimants deposed, and on 26 June 1409 elected Peter Philarghi of Crete, who took the name Alexander V.

But the two deposed popes refused to yield, so that the Church now suffered three claimants instead of two. The Pisan line is today reckoned among the antipopes. Only the Council of Constance would at last heal the schism in 1417 with the election of Martin V.
